topic: Properties of Materials and Their Uses or Harmful Effects
key_concepts: Physical properties can be observed or measured without changing the composition of matter
Chemical properties are shown when a material chemically acts with another material.
Hardness or durability is the ability of a material to resist pressure.
Brittleness is the ability of a material to break easily.
Malleability is the ability of a material to be hammered into flat sheets.
Ductility is the ability of a material to be drawn into thin wires.
Flexibility is the ability of a material to bend without breaking.
Elasticity is the ability of a material to stretch and return to its original shape.
Conductivity is the ability of a material to allow heat and electricity to pass through it
Porosity is the ability of a material to absorb or suck up water.
Transparency is the ability of a material to allow light to pass through.
Flammability is the ability of a material to ignite or catch fire easily.
